# The rise of copyright trolling | Open Rights Group

[Blog](https://www.openrightsgroup.org/blog/) The rise of copyright trolling

#### [Free expression online](https://www.openrightsgroup.org/category/free-expression-online)

## The rise of copyright trolling

## Copyright trolling and speculative invoicing are back in fashion, thanks to tools that can match images and automate the creation of claims of infringement. This has been going on for a while, so it is not too surprising that ORG has received a demand from [PicRights](https://picrights.com/en-gb/), concerning the reproduction of a Facebook ad.

They claim that this reproduction of an image in an advert infringes a copyright. This is a business model which relies on them asking for a sum of £400, in the hope that the recipient doesn’t take legal advice and just pays up. As legal advice might easily cost a larger sum, many recipients will simply pay up.

In our case, the image falls under fair dealing, as it is used for criticism and review. We explain this in [a letter we have sent to them](https://www.openrightsgroup.org/app/uploads/2026/05/Letter_to_PicRights.pdf), which we are publishing in case others fall foul of this kind of practice. Others have apparently ignored them, or offered lower sums of money.

More widely, PicRights and speculative invoicing bring copyright into disrepute. They are not a legal firm. They do not represent the copyright holder directly, but rather they have bought a licence to chase other people for payment. By failing to check if the recipient may have a legitimate defence, and failing to mention the existence of defences, they hope to frighten people into payment.

The legal system should be able to stop activities like this, where companies regularly issue bullying or unfounded requests. Reputation management companies indulge in similar activities, similarly often without genuine legal foundations to their demands. Yet currently, there is no means to fine such companies or otherwise stop this behaviour.

We are aware of at least one other organisation who has recently received a similar letter from another company and wishes to respond: if you are a lawyer and willing to help with their dispute, please email us and we will put you in touch.

# 版權勒索式索賠再度興起

## 版權勒索式索賠與試探式開帳索賠又流行起來了。這要歸功於可以比對圖片、並自動產生侵權主張的工具。這種情況已經持續一段時間，所以 ORG 收到 [PicRights](https://picrights.com/en-gb/) 針對一則 Facebook 廣告重製內容提出的索賠要求，也不算太令人意外。

他們聲稱，在廣告中重製這張圖片侵犯了著作權。這是一種商業模式：他們要求對方支付 400 英鎊，期待收件人不會尋求法律意見，而是直接付錢了事。由於法律諮詢本身很可能就會花掉更多錢，許多收件人最後會選擇直接付款。

以我們的案例來說，這張圖片屬於公平處理（fair dealing）的範圍，因為它被用於批評與評論。我們在[寄給他們的信](https://www.openrightsgroup.org/app/uploads/2026/05/Letter_to_PicRights.pdf)中說明了這一點；我們也公開這封信，以免其他人遇上這類做法時不知道如何因應。據說也有人選擇不理會他們，或提出較低的金額。

更廣泛來看，PicRights 和試探式開帳索賠會讓著作權制度蒙羞。他們不是律師事務所。他們也不是直接代表著作權人，而是購買授權，藉此追討他人的付款。他們沒有查核收件人是否可能有正當的抗辯理由，也沒有提及抗辯理由的存在，而是希望把人嚇到付錢。

法律制度應該能夠阻止這類活動，特別是當公司經常發出霸凌式或毫無根據的要求時。聲譽管理公司也會從事類似活動，而且它們的要求同樣常常沒有真正的法律基礎。然而目前並沒有手段可以對這類公司開罰，或以其他方式阻止這種行為。

我們知道，最近至少還有另一個組織收到另一家公司寄來的類似信件，並希望作出回應：如果你是律師，且願意協助他們處理這起爭議，請寄信給我們，我們會協助你們取得聯繫。
